title: finding: check-changeset-presence counts only a package's own `src/` subtree, so `apps/console/index.html` — shipped and executable — can change with no changeset required
body:
Observation-class finding, noticed while working #5660 (PR #5732). Not fixed there — that PR declares a changeset anyway, because it also touches files under `apps/console/src/`.

## What was measured

`scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs:416` decides whether a changed file counts as package source with:

```js
if (path.startsWith(`${directory}/src/`)) {
```

So the gate's population is each package directory plus `/src/`. `apps/console/index.html` is not under `src/`, and the gate's own summary line confirms it does not count — on PR #5732, which changed four files including `index.html`:

```
Compared the working tree with d8afbe519 (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed,
2 of them under the src/ of a package the release covers, 0 under a package changesets
ignores, 1 changeset(s) added.
```

Three files, two counted — `main.tsx` and the test. `index.html` is not in the count.

## Why that surface is worth a second look

`apps/console/index.html` is not an incidental config file. It is the console's HTML entry, it ships in the package's built `dist`, and it carries **two inline classic scripts that run in every user's browser during parse** — the pre-boot branding/`runtime/config` script and the `crypto.randomUUID` shim for insecure origins. Both are graded by tests precisely because they are shipped behaviour (`src/__tests__/runtimeConfigBootDedup.test.ts` and `src/__tests__/insecure-origin-crypto.test.ts` each extract and execute the real script text).

A PR editing only that file would change shipped console behaviour while the changeset gate stays silent.

## What this is not

The `src/`-only scope looks deliberate for the case the script documents at `:87` — a `package.json` dependency bump should not demand a changeset. The header does not discuss HTML entry points, so whether `index.html` was considered and excluded, or simply never came up, is not recorded. That is the open question; this is not an assertion that the gate is wrong.

If it is intentional, the rationale is worth a sentence in the script header, since the file it lets through is executable shipped code.

## Search-before-file caveat

`search_issues` was returning `total_count: 0` for every query during this session, **including a control term known to exist** — so those zero-hit searches are not readings. (The same degradation is why #5660 itself was filed by the PM on behalf of a dev agent whose search step was blocked.) `list_issues` worked; I scanned the titles of the 100 most recently updated open issues (of 226) and found nothing covering this. Coverage of the older 126 is therefore unverified — close as a duplicate without ceremony if one exists.
